scale.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/fa.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000000000: << میلیارد" and "1000000000000: << هزار میلیارد": میلیارد is 10^9 and 10^12 is a thousand of them, the short-scale values.

group_mark.source: CLDR main/fa.xml, latn symbols inherited from root: group ",".

decimal_mark.source: CLDR main/fa.xml, latn symbols inherited from root: decimal ".".

space_groups.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/fa.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000000000000000000: =#,##0=;": digits are grouped with a mark, not a space.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: en.wiktionary "میلیون": "( plural میلیون‌ها ( milyun-hâ, melyun-hâ ) )"; fa.wikipedia "دستور زبان فارسی": "-ها زمانی استفاده می‌شود که اسم معرفه باشد و پیش از آن عدد نباشد." (the plural in -ها stands with no number before it, so it names no count).

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/fa.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000000: << میلیون[ و >>]": میلیون keeps the singular after every count; fa.wikipedia "دستور زبان فارسی": "شکل‌های جمع پس از اعداد یا صفت‌های زیاد یا بسیاری پدیدار نمی‌شوند." (plural forms do not stand after numbers).

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/fa.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "100: صد[ و >>]".

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/fa.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: << هزار[ و >>]".

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/fa.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: << هزار[ و >>]": و goes before any rest after a thousand, a round hundred too.

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/fa.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: << هزار[ و >>]" writes و and no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/fa.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: << هزار[ و >>]": و goes before any rest after a thousand, so a last group below a hundred or a round hundred with no و starts a new number.

ordinal_style.source: en.wiktionary "یکم": "بیست و یکم ― bist o yekom ― twenty- first"; en.wiktionary "ـمین": "بیست و یکمین ― bist-o yek -omin ― twenty-fir st": the ordinal suffix goes on the last word.

fold_marks.source: en.wiktionary "اول" writes the same word with and without short-vowel marks: "Ordinal : اَوَّل ( avval )" and "اول • ( avval )"; en.wikipedia "Persian alphabet": "Persian script has adopted a subset of Arabic diacritics"; en.wikipedia "Arabic diacritics": "Tashkīl is optional to represent missing vowels and consonant length."

letter_folds.source: en.wikipedia "Persian alphabet", "Deviations from the Arabic script", gives the Persian and Arabic letters side by side: "ی ye U+06CC ي [ b ] U+064A" and "ک kâf U+06A9 ك U+0643"; en.wikipedia, article Yāʼ: "Traditionally, in its isolated and final forms, the letter does not have dots ( ی ), much like the Arabic Alif maqṣūrah"; en.wikipedia "Arabic diacritics": "The same unification of yā and alif maqṣūrā has happened in Persian".

word_chars.source: en.wikipedia "Zero-width non-joiner": "Persian uses this character extensively for certain prefixes, suffixes and compound words."; en.wikipedia "Persian alphabet": "On a computer, they are separated from the word using the zero-width non-joiner"; en.wiktionary "سی": "Ordinal : سی‌ام ( siom )".

bidi_controls.source: CLDR main/fa.xml writes the minus sign with a left-to-right mark before it: "<minusSign>‎−</minusSign>".

native_digits.source: CLDR main/fa.xml: "<defaultNumberingSystem>arabext</defaultNumberingSystem>"; en.wikipedia "Persian alphabet": "Persian uses the Eastern Arabic numerals", "All the digits also have different codepoints in Unicode", "۰ صفر sefr U+06F0 ٠ U+0660"; en.wikipedia "Eastern Arabic numerals": "The Arabic decimal separator ٫ (U+066B)", "The Arabic thousands separator ٬ (U+066C)".

range_cue.source: en.wiktionary "بین": "بین این دو ― bayn-i īn du / beyn-e in do ― between these two".

article_one.source: en.wikipedia "Persian grammar": "The indefinite article in both spoken and literary Persian is the same as the word for 1, یک yek"; "روی میز یک کتاب است".
